prompt.title: Teach it to learn it
prompt.text: For each chapter, pick the one idea you most want to keep. Put it in your own words. Then plan to explain it to someone in the next two days. Teaching it is how you really learn it.
prompt.whyItMatters: Explaining an idea out loud shows what you really understood, and what you only recognised. A name and a date turn a good intention into something you'll do.

form.keyIdeaPrompt: What's the one idea from this chapter you most want to keep? Put it in your own words.
form.personPrompt: Who could you explain it to in the next two days?
form.learnedPrompt: What did explaining it show you?
form.keyIdeaPlaceholder: e.g. How I see a problem shapes what I do. So I check how I see it first.
form.learnedPlaceholder: e.g. Explaining it showed me I couldn't give an example from my own life yet.

chapter.h2: Habit 2: Begin with the end in mind
chapter.h5: Habit 5: Seek first to understand, then to be understood

checklist.planned: Plan one chapter with a date

guide.inShort: You'll write one chapter's key idea in your own words. Then you'll plan who to explain it to, and when. About five minutes, plus a short chat in the next two days. You'll end with a name and a date, and later, what teaching it showed you.
howTo: Pick a chapter you've read from the list.
Write the one idea you most want to keep, in your own words.
Write who you'll explain it to, and set the date.
Once you've explained it, set the status to "Shared".
Write what explaining it showed you.
Tap "Mark done" once one chapter is shared.
